title: Thin 67
subtitle: A 67-key case made of six flat sheets, cut on a laser
role: Design, drawings for making, and the build
summary: A 67-key keyboard whose case is a stack of clear acrylic sheets, each drawn as its own part and cut on a laser. It stands on feet made of cut pieces held by a cross bolt, with a lettered panel under the base.

sections.heading: A case made of sheets
sections.body:
The case is built from flat acrylic sheet. Each layer is drawn as its own part and cut on a laser, then the sheets are fastened together around the switch plate. From the top: a 5 mm top sheet, the 1.5 mm switch plate, a 2 mm layer frosted on one side, a 5 mm clear layer, an 8 mm clear frame and a 2 mm clear base.

It is shown taken apart below. Drag the line back to put it together, or on to the feet. The bought parts lift off first, then the sheets I drew.

sections.heading: The same drawings in other sheet
sections.body: The build is clear acrylic, with one layer frosted on one side. The same drawings can be cut from other sheet. These are renders of the case in three other materials, from the same position and in the same light; they are studies, not builds.

sections.heading: Cut and built
sections.body: The sheets were cut and the board was assembled and used.
